patterns.name: Toccata in D minor: the opening

research.work: J. S. Bach, Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565

research.notes: From the edition’s upper part, bar 1; the left hand doubles it an octave down. The run is in sixty-fourth notes, finer than the sequencer’s thirty-second grid, so the pattern writes every value twice as long at twice the tempo, which plays the same. The file plays the first A without the mordent the score marks on it. The score is a tier-1 source for Bach’s notes, but not for an organist’s part: a recording’s octaves, ornaments, tempo and phrasing are the player’s, and only a listen can say how far they differ. So it is a starting point like any other lead here, and the pattern is _In the style of_. The file’s tempo is 60, the engraver’s, not a marking of the composer’s; the pattern plays at 120 because its values are doubled. Not checked by ear: the owner’s listen is the by-ear step (ruling, 2026-11-01).
